note: Omni and MiniCPM-V rows come from the replayed captures above plus the live run. Super-VL's accuracy/latency columns are scripts/eval_model.py (16 documents x 2 runs, 2026-10-21); its Verdicts column is scripts/live_super_verify.py (3 demo shipments + the 19-group planted bundle, consensus off and on, each twice, 2026-10-23). These rows are data, not prose in the generator.
interpretation: Super-VL was promoted against a written rule and did not clear it. Across all four live passes it reached **3 / 3** shipment verdicts with **0** invented fields -- both bar criteria met -- but scored **74 / 75 (98.7%)** fields exact on the demo documents, reproducibly the same single miss every time, where omni is 75 / 75. The rule required exact >= 99%, so omni stays the default vision model and Super-VL remains selectable. Verbatim drifted between passes (71 to 73 of 75) while compare_key exact did not move at all: the model transcribes loosely and the deterministic layer absorbs it, which is the whole design thesis stated as a number. Its own earlier ceiling bug was ours, not the model's: 1600 completion tokens left a reasoning model no room to write the object, so app/client.py now grants one headroom retry when a response ends exactly on the ceiling; that took the parse rate from 7 of 16 to 16 of 16. Omni dollars are an estimate because NVIDIA publishes no per-token rate; Nebius dollars use the catalog prices in `scripts/spend.py`. The miss is a transcription error, not a hallucination: on the conflict invoice a page printing `PO 4410-DE` came back as `PO 410-DE`, one digit short, and it is the `po_number` field that the replayed capture scores 0/1 exact. Every pass lost exactly one field on that shipment (24/25), so the same reading is unlikely to be coincidence; it is not proven to be the same field, because each pass made its own live call and only the capture run kept a per-field record.
